report:
Fresh reassessment of meta.anchors.test_references: current complete claim, both implementation entries and five ordinary tests. Whole-file inputs include registration, target loading, name parsing and ignored-test helpers; test source/index helpers were additionally captured. No TODO/N/A entries. No source edits, build or tests run. Latest association-only changes do not alter the inspected reference validation; full claim accounting follows rather than reusing a verdict.

Reference validity: correspondence::record_tests recognizes sage::test attributes, parses exactly one dot-separated ASCII anchor name, requires a module-level Function with built-in #[test], rejects functions nested inside another function, requires target.test and standard harness eligibility, and rejects unconditional or recursively cfg_attr-wrapped ignore. Each accepted attribute appends its own site to that rule's vector, so repeated attributes can associate one test with multiple rules and multiple sites can associate with one rule. It applies no crate-ownership restriction. spec::validate_test_references then checks every rule key against the specification inventory and reports each dangling site's annotation span, independently of missing-rule test coverage. Thus correspondence syntax/placement errors and unresolved specification references remain distinct errors.

Target/context helpers: Cargo target loading combines metadata's test flag with parsed manifest harness settings and carries that context into module traversal, including integration support modules. The record path retains target/crate/file identity. AnchorName consumes the full attribute argument stream and validates each component; potentially_ignored recursively checks cfg_attr branches rather than assuming a condition is disabled. These helpers are in the captured correspondence file and were re-inspected.

All five tests: cargo_discovers_unit_and_integration_tests_and_excludes_disabled_harnesses creates a real package with unit, integration and support-module tests plus test=false and harness=false targets. It requires exactly three indexed rules with correct targets/files and exactly two target-eligibility diagnostics. ignored_tests_cannot_supply_specification_coverage checks plain, reasoned, conditional and nested conditional ignore forms, requiring no indexed tests and an ignored diagnostic. test_annotations_reject_malformed_names_and_unsupported_placements checks empty/path/comma/string/raw/non-ASCII/numeric malformed arguments and helper/struct/module/method/nested-function/nested-module/alternate-adapter placements; each requires no entry and the specific validation diagnostic. tests_from_different_crates_can_reference_the_same_specification_rule asserts two distinct crate sites for one library rule and successful validation. test_coverage_is_bidirectional_and_allows_many_to_many_links supplies several sites for a rule and the same test identity across rules, validates them, then creates missing coverage and a dangling typo and checks both diagnostics including the typo annotation span. The many-to-many synthetic test validates inventory semantics; the source registration loop visibly supplies the corresponding multi-attribute construction mechanism. Together these cover every qualification of eligibility, multiplicity, cross-crate use and dangling/misplaced rejection. No concrete new defect or requested edit found.
